text:
Here is the step-by-step reasoning for each problem:

**[id 60]** 
Out of 25 oranges, 1 is bad, 20% of 25 (which is 5) are unripe, and 2 are sour. 
The number of good oranges is: 25 - 1 - 5 - 2 = 17.

**[id 61]** 
The cost to make the brooch is $500 (materials) + $800 (jeweler) = $1,300. 
Insurance is 10% of $1,300 = $130. 
Total money paid: $1,300 + $130 = $1,430.

**[id 62]** 
She is eligible for 5% of her pension for every year worked starting after 20 years. 
Since she worked for 30 years, she has accumulated 10 years of eligibility (30 - 20 = 10). 
10 years × 5% = 50% of the pension value. 
50% of $50,000 = $25,000.

**[id 63]** 
In the first half of the year (6 months), she paid $140/month: 6 × $140 = $840. 
In the second half, the price was 10% less ($140 - $14 = $126). 
For the next 6 months, she paid: 6 × $126 = $756. 
Total paid = $840 + $756 = $1,596.

**[id 64]** 
Sophia drove 100 miles on 4 gallons, which means her car gets 100 / 4 = 25 miles per gallon. 
With a full tank of 12 gallons, she can drive 12 × 25 = 300 miles.

**[id 65]** 
Each time, Jim spends 2 hours watching TV and 1 hour reading (half of 2), totaling 3 hours. 
He does this 3 times a week, meaning he spends 3 × 3 = 9 hours per week. 
In 4 weeks, he spends 9 × 4 = 36 hours.

**[id 66]** 
There are 4 schools. 
Each school sent 2 teams (boys and girls), and each team has 5 players and 1 coach (6 people per team). 
People per school = 2 teams × 6 people/team = 12. 
Total people sent by all 4 schools = 4 × 12 = 48.

**[id 67]** 
Diamonds = 175. 
Rubies = 175 - 35 = 140. 
Emeralds = 140 × 2 = 280. 
Total gems = 175 + 140 + 280 = 595.

**[id 68]** 
Girls = 60. 
Boys = 60 × 2 = 120. 
Total students = 60 + 120 = 180. 
With 5 students per teacher, the number of teachers is 180 / 5 = 36.

**[id 69]** 
Bailey received $5/week for 8 weeks, totaling $40 from her allowance. 
If she ended up with $100, she must have started with $100 - $40 = $60.
